chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fudaylah ibn Ayyub from Dawud ibn Farqad from his father who said:

Hafs al-A'war wrote to me: 'Ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about three issues.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What are they?' He said: 'One who misses fasting three days in a month.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Due to illness or old age or thirst?' He said: 'Explain to me one by one.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is due to illness, then when he recovers, let him make up for it; and if it is due to old age or thirst, then for each day, one mudd [of food].'

key_terms.مُدٌّ: A specific measure of volume for food (fidya)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between making up missed fasts and paying fidya for the elderly or ill in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between temporary impediments, such as illness, which necessitate qada (making up the fast), and permanent or chronic conditions like old age, which require fidya (expiation) of one mudd of food per day. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the specific etiology of the missed fast in determining the appropriate form of compensation, reflecting the nuanced application of Quranic verses on fasting.
